phrasings.literal: How many findings are there about the sections of plan #254?

gold_query: MATCH (f:finding) WHERE EXISTS { (f)-[:ABOUT]->(s) WHERE s IN subtree(#254) } RETURN count(*)

trap.lure: counts the bindings of (f:finding)-[:ABOUT]->(s) with count(*), one per finding-section pair, instead of one per finding

notes: SD §6: findings #501-#504 and #801-#803 are about sections of #254 (7); #502 and #803 are each about two sections, so the fixed pattern binds 9 times ([50 §3.4] items 1 and 6).

phrasings.literal: How many tasks in the tree of #240 have at least one direct prerequisite, a task or question that must finish before them, whatever that prerequisite's status?

gold_query: MATCH (t:task) WHERE t IN subtree(#240) AND EXISTS { (b)-[:BLOCKS]->(t) } RETURN count(*)

trap.lure: counts the bindings of ()-[:BLOCKS]->(t) for t in the tree with count(*), one per prerequisite link, instead of one per task

notes: SD §6: BLOCKS edges into #240's tree are #241->#243, #243->#244, #241->#245, #243->#245, #242->#246, #245->#246, #225->#247, #245->#248, #252->#251 (9) with 7 distinct targets; #249 and #250 are blocked only by inheritance and have no direct in-edge.

phrasings.literal: How many tasks on main have at least one subtask?

trap.lure: counts the bindings of (c:task)<-[:CHILD_OF]-() with count(*), one per child, instead of one per parent task

notes: SD §5.3-§5.6 and §6: the task parents on main are #240 (13 children), #248 (2), #260 (7), #273 (8) and #285 (4); no filler task has a CHILD_OF edge, so 5 parents and 34 child edges.

phrasings.literal: Counting each link once, how many direct prerequisite links make up the chains of prerequisites that end at #280?

gold_query: MATCH (a)-[:BLOCKS]->(b) WHERE b = #280 OR EXISTS { (b)-[:BLOCKS]->+(#280) } RETURN count(*)

trap.lure: counts count(*) over (x)-[:BLOCKS]->+(#280), which binds the 3 upstream endpoint pairs, not the links on the chains

notes: SD §6: the chains into #280 use #274->#280, #275->#280, #276->#280 and #274->#275 (4 links); #276->#277 does not lead to #280. Upstream endpoints are #274, #275, #276 (3).

phrasings.literal: How many tasks in the tree of #240 sit below at least one other task of that tree?

trap.lure: counts (x:task)-[:CHILD_OF]->+(y) with y in #240's tree, which binds one (task, ancestor) endpoint pair each: 15 pairs with #240 plus 2 with #248

notes: SD §5.3 and §6: #240 has 13 children and #248 has #249 and #250, so 15 tasks sit below #240 (every task of the tree except #240); #249 and #250 have two ancestors in the tree, giving 17 endpoint pairs.

phrasings.literal: What fraction of the round-1 findings about sections of plan #254 ended up refuted, as a number between 0 and 1?

gold_query: MATCH (f:finding) WHERE f.round = 1 AND EXISTS { (f)-[:ABOUT]->(s) WHERE s IN subtree(#254) } RETURN count(CASE WHEN f.status = 'refuted' THEN 1 END) / count(*) AS share

trap.lure: expects integer division (Cypher's 1 / 4 = 0) and truncates the quotient, e.g. toInteger(refuted / raised), giving 0

notes: SD §5.9 and §6: round-1 findings about #255-#259 are #501-#504, of which only #502 is refuted: 1 / 4 = 0.25, a float in LQ ([50 §3.3]).

phrasings.literal: What priority does the jitter buffer task #1402 have?

trap.lure: reads #1402 on the default view main, where it was never merged: 0 rows

notes: SD §4 and §5.5: #1402 (TC-10, P1) was created by c.net-new-tasks on lane/net and exists only there; on main it yields no row and N06 naming lane/net ([50 §3.6]).
